traceability.evidence:
1) Implementation: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts - Implements deep validation of @req and @supports annotations against story file requirements. - Parses story markdown contents and extracts requirement IDs via `const regex = /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g;` in loadAndCacheRequirements, so any `REQ-...` pattern in any section or list format is supported (satisfying REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION). - Caches requirement IDs per story file using `Map<string, Set>` (REQ-DEEP-CACHE), so each story file is only read and parsed once per lint run. - Validates that each @req line refers to an existing requirement in the current storyPath via validateReqLine and checkRequirementExists; similar validation is applied for each requirement ID listed after an @supports line via validateImplementsLine (REQ-DEEP-MATCH). - Performs path safety checks (no `..`, no absolute paths, and must remain inside cwd) in validateAndResolveStoryPath, and reports `invalidPath` instead of throwing, covering error handling and integration with file validation. - Provides clear, specific error messages in meta.messages: `reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'` and `invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'`, including both the requirement ID and story path for context (REQ-DEEP-ERROR & user experience). - Integrates with existing annotation parsing by scanning all comments via processAllComments, recognizing @story, @req, and @supports lines in handleAnnotationLine, and maintaining a current storyPath across lines and comments.
2) Plugin integration: src/index.ts - The rule is registered under RULE_NAMES as "valid-req-reference" and dynamically loaded from ./rules/valid-req-reference, so ESLint can use it. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES includes "traceability/valid-req-reference": "error", and createTraceabilityFlatConfig plus configs.recommended/strict expose this rule in the plugin configs, showing it is integrated with the existing validation rule set.
3) Tests: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts with fixtures - Test file is explicitly tied to this story: header contains `Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` and `@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md`. - Valid cases: • Uses a real story markdown file docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md with `// @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE`; that REQ exists in the story file, verifying basic deep match. • Uses tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md containing `- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format`, verifying support for bullet-list requirement formatting. • Uses tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md with lists containing REQ-SHARED-ID and per-file unique requirements, validated via @supports lines, confirming handling of multi-story usage and requirement ID scoping. - Invalid cases: • Missing requirement in a real story file (`REQ-NON-EXISTENT`) asserts an error with messageId "reqMissing" and correct reqId/storyPath data. • Path traversal and absolute path scenarios for both @story and @supports assert "invalidPath" with the offending storyPath. • Missing bullet requirement in story_bullet.md and missing @supports requirements in multi-story fixtures assert the proper `reqMissing` messages. - These tests directly exercise core functionality, quality standards (various formats and structures), integration with existing annotation semantics, user-facing error messages, and error handling for bad paths.
4) Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md - Document is annotated with `@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` and requirements like REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-PATH. - Describes exactly what the rule does: parses story files, extracts requirement IDs, validates each @req and @supports ID, reports `invalidPath` and `reqMissing`, and explains that requirement IDs are scoped per story file. - Provides concrete examples covering correct and incorrect usages, including multi-story @supports and path traversal/absolute path cases, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion with clear examples of supported formats and behaviors.
5) Test run evidence - Command: `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose`. - Output includes: `PASS tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts` under `Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)` with all valid and invalid scenarios passing. - Global summary: `Test Suites: 36 passed, 36 total; Tests: 272 passed, 272 total`, confirming the deep validation behavior is fully tested and currently passing.
traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md defines deep requirement validation that must (1) verify @req references actually correspond to requirement identifiers present in story files, (2) handle different markdown formats and structures, (3) integrate with existing annotation parsing and file validation, (4) provide clear error messages, (5) handle malformed or unsafe paths safely, and (6) be documented with examples.
The implemented ESLint rule src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts fulfills these requirements: it parses story files once per file and caches discovered REQ identifiers, supports multiple markdown structures by scanning the entire file with a regex for REQ- patterns, validates both @req and @supports annotations against those IDs, and integrates with existing annotation semantics through a Program-level visitor that walks all comments. It includes robust path validation that prevents traversal/absolute paths and reports them via a dedicated error message instead of throwing, and emits precise error messages when requirements are missing, including both the missing ID and the associated story path.
Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts (plus the supporting fixtures) cover successful and failing scenarios across real stories, bullet-list fixtures, and multi-story fixtures, and assert the exact error messages and data. The plugin exports and config wiring in src/index.ts ensure the rule is available and enabled in recommended/strict presets. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md clearly explains the behavior and provides examples matching the implementation.
Given this evidence and the passing test suite, all acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied, so the story is fully implemented.
